About

Ten years of keeping businesses steady — now doing it with AI.

I'm a remote Operations & Project Management professional with ten years of experience across US-based client teams — running day-to-day operations, building the systems that keep teams on schedule, and acting as the main point of contact between leadership, clients, and internal teams. While my experience so far has been with US-based teams, I'm open to working with clients anywhere in the world.

I'm ClickUp Certified, and over the past couple of years I've been extending that same systems-thinking into AI: building automations on Make.com with live APIs, custom Claude/GPT-powered tools, and Google Apps Script reporting that removes manual work entirely rather than just organizing it.

AI / Automation Desk

Where AI meets real business systems.

Custom Claude-powered tools, live Make.com automations built on real APIs, and Google Apps Script reporting — built to remove manual work, not just organize it.

AI Desk · 1 of 9
SOP Generator — a Claude-powered internal tool
What it is: A Claude project that takes a pasted Loom transcript and turns it into a structured, execution-ready Standard Operating Procedure. Result: SOP writing dropped from hours to minutes, with a consistent format every time.
AI Desk · 2 of 9
Custom RAG policy chatbot — built for a client
What it is: An AI assistant trained only on a client's internal content policy, with suggested questions and a scoped knowledge base (company name blurred for confidentiality). Result: Employees get instant, accurate policy answers without pinging HR every time.
AI Desk · 3 of 9
Same chatbot — answering in real time
What it is: The assistant cites the exact policy section for an in-scope question, and correctly declines a question the policy doesn't cover instead of guessing. Result: Grounded, hallucination-resistant behavior — not just a chat wrapper on top of an LLM.
AI Desk · 4 of 9
Make.com automation — client onboarding, built on live APIs
What it is: A webhook-triggered scenario that creates ClickUp tasks, Drive folders, and Slack notifications automatically when a new client form comes in. Result: New client onboarding went from a manual multi-step checklist to a single automatic flow.
AI Desk · 5 of 9
Make.com automation — branching campaign routing
What it is: A router-based scenario that sends one form submission down the correct path, updates ClickUp, and notifies the right Slack channel depending on campaign type. Result: Removed manual routing decisions and eliminated missed handoffs between campaigns.
AI Desk · 6 of 9
From script to live tracker
What it is: A config-driven Google Apps Script automation that pulls data straight from the Slack API on a schedule and rebuilds a Response Time Tracker spreadsheet automatically — the code on the left produces the live tracker on the right. Result: A self-refreshing system with no manual data entry; a weekly trigger keeps it current on its own.
AI Desk · 7 of 9
One system, five trackers
What it is: The same automation approach applied across five different trackers — Email, Meetings, ClickUp, and Client Documentation among them — each with its own config, cadence, and rules. Result: One consistent, scalable reporting system instead of five one-off spreadsheets. (The Client Touchpoints tracker shown here is the same one behind the "catching a bad number before reporting it" story earlier in this portfolio.)
AI Desk · 8 of 9
Prototyping with AI before automating
What it is: Tested the Slack API logic in Python first — pulling real conversation threads, checking reply structures, pagination, and rate-limit handling — refining the approach with AI-assisted prototyping before converting it into production Apps Script. Result: Fewer surprises once the automation went live, because the edge cases were already worked out.
AI Desk · 9 of 9
Keeping every build organized and documented
What it is: Each automation gets its own scoped Claude project — a clear description of its purpose and what it rebuilds — instead of scattered one-off scripts. Result: Easy to hand off, revisit, or extend months later without having to reverse-engineer old work.
Ops Desk

Catching problems before they go live.

Ten years of ClickUp-based operations work — including flagging system-design issues in automation logic before they cause bad data downstream, and building a live KPI Team Dashboard system that tracks workload, task completion, and on-time performance across the whole team.

Ops Desk · 1 of 7
Catching a labeling conflict before it caused bad data
What it is: Flagged that three ClickUp forms feeding into one shared list would create labeling conflicts in the connected Make.com automation, before it caused any bad data. Result: Proposed and implemented a fix (a required "Form Type" field) that prevented a production bug before it happened.
Ops Desk · 2 of 7
KPI Team Dashboard — the full suite
What it is: A dashboard system built inside ClickUp — one individual task dashboard per team member, plus a shared Team Overview, all organized in one library. Result: Anyone on the team (or leadership) can check workload and status in one place instead of digging through task lists.
Ops Desk · 3 of 7
Individual dashboard — due dates & on-time rate
What it is: A personal dashboard showing tasks due in the next 7 days, total open tasks, completed-late count, on-time completion rate, and a live task list. Result: Each team member can self-check their own load and standing without asking a manager.
Ops Desk · 4 of 7
Team Overview — workload & overdue tracking
What it is: Open tasks by assignee and overdue tasks by assignee, charted side by side, plus a "Who's Behind" list ranked by overdue notifications. Result: Bottlenecks and uneven workload are visible at a glance, before they become missed deadlines.
Ops Desk · 5 of 7
On-time performance — tracked per person
What it is: On-time completion percentage calculated and displayed per team member, refreshed automatically. Result: Performance conversations are backed by a live number, not a guess.
Ops Desk · 6 of 7
Learning an unfamiliar system, then documenting it for the team
What it is: Tested three GHL-to-ClickUp automation forms (New Campaign, Onboarding, Re-Launch) end to end, then wrote a plain-language breakdown of what each one triggers for the team to actually use. Result: Caught and diagnosed a specific formula error before it affected a real client, with the exact fix identified.
Ops Desk · 7 of 7
Refining a system through a stakeholder's questions — and catching a bad number before reporting it
What it is: Built a response-time tracker across Slack and ClickUp, refining the rules through a stakeholder’s detailed edge-case questions (self-replies, reaction-only messages, unanswered tags). Result: A consistent, edge-case-proof system — and before reporting a number showing 100% of clients missing documentation, flagged it as suspicious and asked where the real source of truth was, instead of reporting a figure that might have been wrong.
